extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, regulated parties, researchers, and stakeholders searching the Federal Register for cannabis-related notices, rules, and publications
extracted.subtask_description: Search-results listing of Federal Register documents matching the term 'cannabis', aggregating notices, rules, proposed rules, and abstracts across multiple agencies that concern cannabis, hemp, controlled-substance scheduling, and related regulatory programs. Useful for finding rulemaking dockets, guidance, registration notices, and information-collection requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics FDA solicits for comments on cannabis-derived products in veterinary practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The FDA is soliciting comments, particularly from veterinarians, on the use of cannabis-derived products (CDPs) in animals with emphasis on cannabidiol (CBD) products and general trends associated with those products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically requests information about: usage trends (e.g., product selection, indications, etc.), quality standards, benefits of use, potential drug interactions, adverse events and safety problems, and toxicological concerns. (Context: FDA Center for Veterinary Medicine request for information.)

rubrics_metrics.name: DEA evaluation standard for bulk-manufacturer / grower registrations (21 CFR part 1318 / 21 CFR 1301.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: DEA will evaluate applications to be registered to manufacture in bulk or to grow marihuana for scientific and medical research according to its regulations governing the program (see rule at 85 FR 82333 and 21 CFR part 1318).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 21 CFR 1301.33(a) and 21 CFR 1318.05(b)(3)(ii), the Agency considers whether the applicant possesses registration as a Schedule I researcher with respect to marihuana, whether the applicant has a bona fide supply agreement with a registered researcher or manufacturer, and the extent to which the applicant is able to supply cannabis or its derivatives in quantities needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA 'Quality Considerations for Clinical Research' topics for cannabis-derived human drugs
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance presents FDA's current thinking on topics relevant to development of cannabis and cannabis-derived human drugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key elements include: the source of cannabis for clinical research; general quality considerations for developing human drugs that contain cannabis and cannabis-derived compounds; and calculation of percent delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) in botanical raw materials, intermediates, drug substances, and drug products to determine their control status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hemp definition and the 0.3% delta-9-THC threshold (2018 Farm Bill / AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: As defined in the 2018 Farm Bill/Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018 (AIA), 'hemp' means Cannabis sativa L. and any part or derivative with a delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol concentration of not more than 0.3 percent on a dry weight basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition covers seeds, derivatives, extracts, cannabinoids, isomers, acids, salts, and salts of isomers, whether growing or not. Material testing above 0.3% THC is treated as marijuana under federal law and triggers different regulatory treatment and reporting (e.g., disposal reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic Hemp Production Program reporting and disposal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: USDA/AMS requires forms and reports for licensed hemp producers and States/Territories/Tribes with approved hemp plans as part of the Domestic Hemp Production Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a form required to be submitted to USDA on the first business day of each month; AMS-24 State and Tribal Hemp Disposal Report requires States/Tribes to provide disposal or remediation information for cannabis that tested above the 0.3% THC threshold, and to include the producer's license number, lot location information (including geospatial location or other land descriptor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Germaneness/scope requirement for public comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments submitted during a rule's public-comment period must raise issues germane to the proposed action; comments outside the scope may be dismissed as not relevant to the specific rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by EPA responses treating comments about environmental effects of cannabis cultivation (VOC/ozone, greenhouse gas emissions) as outside the scope of certain SIP or permitting actions when those actions do not relate to cannabis production. Agencies will note when a comment is outside the action's scope and decline to incorporate it into that docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescheduling standard under the Controlled Substances Act (CSA) and procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfers of substances between schedules of the CSA must be made through formal rulemaking on the record after opportunity for a hearing, and consider HHS findings about whether a substance has a currently accepted medical use and its abuse potential and dependence risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: DOJ proposed transferring marijuana from Schedule I to Schedule III consistent with HHS's view that marijuana has a currently accepted medical use and based on HHS's evaluations of abuse potential and physical/psychological dependence; DOJ solicits comments as part of that rulemaking. If finalized, schedule-specific regulatory controls would apply and other statutory obligations (e.g., FDCA for drugs) would remain in force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of rescheduling FDA-approved marijuana-containing drug products to Schedule III
rubrics_metrics.description: When FDA-approved marijuana-containing products are placed in Schedule III, they are to be regulated under Schedule III CSA controls, and certain import/export and permit requirements apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule placing such products in Schedule III also adds them to the list of substances that may only be imported or exported pursuant to a permit, and establishes an expedited registration process under 21 CFR part 1301 for entities holding state medical marijuana licenses so they may engage in manufacture/distribution/dispensing consistent with treaty and federal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: DEA assignment of specific drug codes and listings for cannabis-related substances
rubrics_metrics.description: DEA may create or amend specific listings and Controlled Substances Code Numbers for particular cannabinoids or analogues to list them explicitly in schedule tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: DEA establishing a specific listing and drug code for hexahydrocannabinol (HHC) in Schedule I because HHC meets the definition of tetrahydrocannabinols; other entries list drug codes for Marihuana Extract (7350), Marihuana (7360), and Tetrahydrocannabinols (7370) as Schedule I substances in notices of registrations/applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope-limited authorizations in DEA registration notices
rubrics_metrics.description: DEA notices for bulk-manufacturer/importer/registrant applications specify the precise activities and substances authorized and explicitly state that no other activities are authorized for that registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: registration may authorize bulk manufacture of listed controlled substances to provide Cannabis as botanical raw material and/or APIs to DEA-registered researchers and manufacturers only; import permits approved only when registrant's business activity is consistent with statutory provisions (e.g., 21 U.S.C. 952(a)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB/PRA information-collection review and public notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must publish notices under the Paperwork Reduction Act when seeking extension/revision of approved information collections, and submit proposed collections to OMB for review and clearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices describe the collection's purpose (e.g., data to support social and behavioral research including use of botanical substances such as cannabis-derived products), the PRA justification, and solicit public comment on the proposed burden and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-comment period timing and procedure (example 30-day period)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies provide a public comment period for proposed actions; in some examples a 30-day comment period was provided for EPA proposed actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The docket will state the period during which comments are accepted; agency responses in final actions often summarize received comments and explain whether and why they were considered germane or rejected.
